Lessons.Title: Types of Angles
ExplanationParagraphs: IM/KH 2021 U07:L12: classify angles acute, obtuse, straight and draw acute/obtuse. The 90-degree right boundary must be treated separately. Original 2021 source had prior local inspection; new direct device read timed out, so use the archived source evidence without inventing original visual answers.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Number Talk: Fractions of 120 and 360 (10 minutes); Activity 1: Sorting Angles (10 minutes); Activity 2: What is It, Really? (10 minutes); Activity 3: Small Angles, Large Angles (15 minutes); Cool-down: Obtuse, Acute, and Straight Angles (5 minutes)
Source warm-up Fractions of 120 and 360: two recorded original Student Facing expressions 12×1/12=1 and 120×1/12=10. Other items were not captured in available excerpt.

Activity 1 Sorting Angles: sort actual paper angle cards created in preceding U07:L11 into two groups and explain why. Teacher measures physical drawings; digital numeric categories are supplementary.

Activity 2 What is It, Really?: original Mai/Jada discuss line-versus-angle, and Tyler/Andre an angle in letter Y. Two opposite rays with one vertex can create 180° straight angle, but source picture measurement remains unverified. Original Activity 3 Small Angles, Large Angles drawing tasks require teacher source review.
First-party cooldown, not gated publisher: classify 45° acute, 130° obtuse, 180° straight. 90° is right. No original publisher original Cool-down copied.

KeyConcepts.Title: Straight
KeyConcepts.Definition: Exactly half of a full turn.
